SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / ARRIVAL & RECEPTION

Complete guide to creative office reception design.

Make the first few minutes feel straightforward. This Space Craft planning note looks at complete guide to creative office reception design through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEFollow the visitor journeySize the setting to actual useExpress identity with restraintMap activity before assigning desksBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Follow the visitor journey

Think through finding the entrance, checking in, waiting and moving to a meeting. Make the next step clear without asking a visitor to cross private working areas.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Size the setting to actual use

Estimate the number of people who may arrive together and the support they need. A generous reception desk is not a substitute for suitable waiting seats, an accessible approach or a place for bags.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Express identity with restraint

A considered sign, a material or a focused colour moment may tell the brand story more effectively than filling every wall. Check the view from both the entrance and the seated waiting position.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Map activity before assigning desks

Write down the tasks people perform, how often teams overlap and when visitors arrive. A desk count alone will not reveal the need for private calls, project tables or storage.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Walk through an unfamiliar visitor’s route.
  • Test seating and desk dimensions at full scale.
  • Keep sign-in information and private documents protected.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.

General design considerations for discussion. Product suitability, technical performance, statutory requirements and project pricing need appropriate, project-specific review. Images are illustrative.
